mem.t: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.

lessons.title: The Meaning of 920
lessons.theme: The self-emptied “0” bearing ninefold fruit in every “2”

v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”
Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
This is the first and great commandment.
A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’

lessons.still: Sit quietly and close your eyes. Let the faces you will meet today slowly come to mind: family, colleagues, brothers and sisters in Christ. Don't rush to evaluate them. Simply bring them one by one before the Lord and whisper, “Lord, this is someone you have entrusted to me.”
teach: A fruit tree never bears fruit for itself: an apple tree doesn't eat its own apples. Fruit is for others to eat and enjoy. In the same way, the fruit of the Spirit is not a spiritual medal locked in a glass case for people to admire; it is the taste of Christ that others experience in their relationships with us. In the first two stages we learned to put down roots and to live the self-emptied life. From this week on, we learn to bear fruit.

Jesus said, “A new commandment I give to you.” Loving our neighbour as ourselves was already in the Old Testament, so what was new? The new thing is the measuring rod: “just as I have loved you.” Moments before saying this, the Lord had stooped down to wash his disciples' feet. The standard of love was raised from “as yourself” to “as I have loved you,” and the source of love shifted from ourselves to the Lord who first loved us. The world would recognise his disciples not by their knowledge but by their love for one another.

920 is the way we practise this new commandment. Every person I am in relationship with is my “2”; I practise the self-emptied life and become a “0”; and I let the Holy Spirit bear the ninefold fruit, the “9”, between me and my “2”. The key is the 0: the less of me, the more of the Lord. I no longer demand that the other person change first; instead I let Christ first live his life out in me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships is first with God, then with ourselves, then with others. 920 is not a social skill but the natural overflow of our relationship with God. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things. God's kingdom system is built precisely out of one “2” after another who has been touched by the Lord's love.
q: Who is God? — Jesus defined love by washing feet. What does this show you about God?
Who am I? — When you have looked at the people around you, have you seen them as your “2”, or as tools, obstacles or background scenery?
How shall I respond? — What one concrete action will you take today to let someone taste the love of Christ?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' whole ministry happened in relationships: he called twelve men to be with him, he talked with a despised woman at a well, and he called Zacchaeus by name from under a tree. He never treated people as tools for getting the work done. In his eyes, every person was someone entrusted to him by the Father, someone worth laying down his life to love.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for loving me first, for stooping to wash my feet and for laying down your life for me. Open my eyes to see that every person around me is a “2” you have given me. Make me a “0”, so that your life flows out through me and bears the fruit of the Spirit in my relationships, and people recognise that I am your disciple. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: reach out with a greeting today and listen attentively to what they say
Write down “just as I have loved you” and put it where you will often see it
Memorise this week's verse: John 13:34
lessons.noon: “Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.” — Lord, right now let me love the person in front of me with your love.

lessons.title: The Vine and the Branches
lessons.theme: A branch doesn't strain to bear fruit; it simply remains in the vine

v: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

lessons.still: Picture yourself as a branch, securely joined to the vine. As you breathe in, pray silently, “Lord, I am in you.” As you breathe out, pray, “You are in me.” Repeat this a few times, and let the security of that connection slowly replace the anxiety and hurry in your heart.
teach: Have you ever heard a grapevine branch “straining” in the night? Of course not. A branch never grits its teeth to squeeze out fruit. It does only one thing: it stays joined to the vine. The sap flows from the root into the branch, and in due season the fruit hangs there in clusters. Many Christians live exhausted lives precisely because they think of themselves as the fruit tree rather than the branch.

In John 15 the word “remain” comes up again and again. It means to settle down and stay, not to drop by for an occasional visit. Jesus said, “Apart from me you can do nothing.” Not “you can do a little less,” but “you can do nothing.” Love, joy and peace are not products the branch manufactures; they are the life of the vine flowing out through the branch.

So the practice of 920 does not begin with trying harder to be nice to people; it begins with coming back to the Lord. When I feel weary and dried up in a relationship, the question is not “How much harder must I try?” but “Have I wandered away from the vine?” Once that mindset changes, the burden lifts: bearing fruit is the Lord's job; remaining is mine.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life is the branch's true place: not treating ourselves as the source, and admitting that apart from the Lord we can do nothing. The self-ruled person wants to be the vine and ends up withered; the self-emptied person is content to be a branch, bears much fruit, and the glory goes to the Father, the gardener.
q: Who is God? — “I am the vine.” Jesus is willing to be the source of your life. What comfort does that give you?
Who am I? — In which relationship are you wearing yourself out trying to “strain out fruit” by your own effort?
How shall I respond? — In what concrete way will you “remain” in the Lord today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus himself is our example of remaining in the Father. He said, “The Son can do nothing of himself.” He often withdrew to lonely places to pray, receiving from the Father and then going back among the crowds to give. Every compassionate act of his flowed naturally out of his union with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are the vine and I am a branch. I confess that apart from you I can do nothing. I lay down my efforts to be good to people in my own strength, and I come back to you. Let your life flow into my heart like sap, so that at home, at work and at church I naturally bear fruit that brings glory to the Father. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pause three times today to pray silently: “Lord, I am in you.”
For one of my 2s: pray for them first, then spend time with them
Write down one relationship that wears you out and hand it over to the vine
lessons.noon: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” — Lord, right now I remain in you.

lessons.title: Nine Fruits, One Life
lessons.theme: The fruit of the Spirit is one whole cluster, not nine separate report cards

v: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.

lessons.still: Slowly read aloud the names of the nine fruits, pausing after each one. Don't examine whether you have it or not; simply say to the Lord, “This is your character.” Let your heart turn from grading yourself to quietly gazing on Christ.
teach: A bunch of grapes has many individual grapes, yet they all grow from the same branch and the same sap. Paul writes “fruit” in the singular. Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control are not nine separate subjects from which we choose the ones we are good at; they are nine facets of one and the same life of Christ.

Compare the verses just before: “the works of the flesh” are plural, things people produce by their own doing. But what the Spirit produces is “fruit”, something that grows out of life. Paul goes on to say that those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh; since we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit. The word “walk” here carries the sense of keeping in step, marching in line: we follow the Spirit's pace.

This brings an important shift in mindset. We cannot have joy without patience, or cultivate gentleness while neglecting faithfulness. If one fruit is especially lacking, it is usually not because we haven't practised that particular virtue enough, but because in that area the self has not yet been surrendered. The answer is not to patch up one character trait but to let Christ live in us more deeply.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fruit is the life of Christ flowing naturally out of a self-emptied person, not the product of self-cultivation. The old self, ruled by self, produces “the works of the flesh”; the new self, emptied of self, bears “the fruit of the Spirit”. The Holy Spirit is my guide, and walking by the Spirit means neither running ahead of him nor lagging behind.
q: Who is God? — Taken together, the nine fruits are a portrait of Jesus. Which aspect of him draws you most?
Who am I? — Have you treated your spiritual life like nine school subjects, showing off only the ones you're good at?
How shall I respond? — In what situation today will you “keep in step with the Spirit”?
lessons.jesus: In Jesus the nine fruits were never divided. He loved sinners yet hated sin; on the cross he endured mockery and still interceded for others; when he cleansed the temple he burned with zeal yet never lost self-control. Jesus himself is that whole cluster of fruit, and what the Spirit wants to bear in us is his likeness.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for living in me. I will no longer treat my spiritual life as a report card of self-improvement. I bring my flesh, with its passions and desires, to the cross. Bear your complete fruit in me, so that people may see the likeness of Jesus in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Copy the nine fruits onto a card and carry it with you today
For one of my 2s: notice which fruit is most lacking today and confess it to the Lord
When conflict comes, pause for three seconds and ask, “Holy Spirit, what is your pace?”
lessons.noon: “If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.” — Lord, right now I keep in step with you.

lessons.title: Bearing Fruit in Relationships
lessons.theme: Fruit is seen and tasted between people

v: For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?

lessons.still: Recall a recent time when you came away from being with someone with unease in your heart. Don't rush to defend yourself or to blame anyone. Just bring that scene before the Lord and say, “Lord, you were there too. Please teach me.”
teach: You can't learn to swim by reading a swimming book on the shore, and you can't learn patience by practising only when you're alone. A hermit living in a cave can easily feel very gentle and very patient, because nobody is getting on his nerves. God has placed us in families, workplaces and churches not to torment us, but to give the fruit a place to grow.

Paul says we were called to freedom, but we must not use our freedom as an opportunity for the flesh; rather, through love we are to serve one another, for the whole law is summed up in one word: “Love your neighbour as yourself.” John puts it even more bluntly: whoever does not love the brother he can see cannot love the God he cannot see. Our relationship with God is the root; our relationships with people are the fruit. If the root is real, the fruit will show up in the lives of others.

So the person you find hardest to bear may be the very orchard God has prepared for you. Our mindset needs to shift from “He is my problem” to “He is my 2, the place where the Lord lets me bear fruit.” The focus is not on the other person's faults, but on whether, right now, I am letting Jesus reign. Life first, then relationships, then ministry.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things; never hurt people for the sake of getting things done. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and both sides win. Relationships are the touchstone of the Spirit's fruit and the building blocks of God's kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God has placed you in these relationships. What does this tell you about his intentions for you?
Who am I? — Do you say you love God while keeping your distance from a brother or sister you can see?
How shall I respond? — With what small act will you “serve through love” someone today?
lessons.jesus: Among the Twelve Jesus chose were impulsive Peter, doubting Thomas and even Judas, who would betray him. He did not pick only the easy people. Through three years of living together day and night he shaped them with love, patience and kindness. His fruit was borne in the most real of relationships.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for placing me among family, colleagues and brothers and sisters in Christ. I confess that I often want to avoid people who are difficult. Help me see that they are exactly where you want me to bear fruit. Today I choose to serve in love and to let you reign in every relationship. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: do one small act of service for them
Write down the name of someone who is hard for you, and beside it write “my 2”
When you disagree with someone today, listen first, then respond
lessons.noon: “But through love be servants to one another.” — Lord, right now let me serve you in this relationship.

lessons.title: My 2 List
lessons.theme: The Lord appoints me to bear fruit, starting with each “2” around me

v: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

lessons.still: Take out a pen and paper and be still for a minute. Ask the Holy Spirit to remind you: Who do I see every day? Who has drifted away from me lately? Who is hard for me to get along with? Let the names surface one by one. Don't write them down yet; just place them in the Lord's hands.
teach: A farmer doesn't say, “I love all the fields in the world.” He tends his own few plots, and he knows which one needs watering and which one needs weeding. It is easy to love “all humanity”; it is not easy to love the one person who lives under the same roof. For the practice of 920 to touch the ground, we need a concrete “My 2 List”.

Jesus said, “You didn't choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit.” Bearing fruit is a mission we are sent on, not a personal hobby. And Paul teaches us how to regard these people: in humility count others better than yourself, and look not only to your own interests but also to the interests of others. This is exactly the posture of the “0”.

This week, please build your list: family members, colleagues at work, spiritual companions at church, people who need care, and the one person you find hardest to love. In each of the coming weeks we will practise one fruit and put it into practice concretely with one “2” on the list. Next week we begin with the first fruit: love.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The spiritual relationships of 235 (2 spiritual companions, 3 spiritual parents and children, 5 fellow soldiers) are all on this list. Our one purpose is to build what belongs to God, and God's kingdom system begins with your willingness to lay yourself down for one “2”, so that Jesus receives all the glory.
q: Who is God? — “I chose you.” The Lord took the initiative to choose you and send you. What assurance does that give you?
Who am I? — Who on your list are you most likely to overlook?
How shall I respond? — Which person on your list will you begin praying for faithfully?
lessons.jesus: In his prayer in John 17 Jesus said, “I revealed your name to the people whom you have given me out of the world.” He knew exactly whom the Father had entrusted to him, and he interceded for them and kept them one by one, until he laid down his life for them.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for choosing me and appointing me to bear fruit. I bring every name on my list before you. Help me see them as you see them. Make me humble in heart, counting others better than myself, and let me live out your love toward each of these 2s. May you receive all the glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write your “My 2 List”, with at least five names
For one of my 2s: pray for them once every day this week
At the weekend, share your list with a spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit.” — Lord, right now I receive your sending.

lessons.title: God Is Love
lessons.theme: We can love because God first loved us

v: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his only born Son into the world that we might live through him.
In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
We love him, because he first loved us.

lessons.still: Rest your open hands on your knees, like an empty cup. Quietly say, “Lord, I have no love in myself. Please pour your love into me.” Then simply receive. Don't hurry to do anything for anyone else; first let yourself be filled with love.
teach: An empty cup cannot pour out water. Many people want to love others but grow drier the more they love, because they keep pouring out and are never filled. Love comes first among the nine fruits because it is the root of all the others; and the root of love is not in us but in God.

John says, “God is love.” He does not mean God is loving some of the time; he means love is God's very nature. How was this love revealed? God sent his one and only Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. John stresses the order: “not that we loved God, but that he loved us,” and again, “We love because he first loved us.” Love always starts on God's side.

So the first step in practising love is not to grit our teeth and love harder, but to be still and receive being loved. Our mindset needs to shift from “I must love” to “I am loved, so I can love.” For someone filled with love, loving others is no longer a chore; it is the natural overflow of a full heart.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-ruled love is a transaction: I'll be good to you if you're good to me. Self-emptied love is an overflow: God loved me first, so I pass that love on. The fruit is the life of Christ flowing naturally out of a self-emptied person, not the product of self-cultivation. The source of love is God, and the glory goes to God.
q: Who is God? — “God is love.” How does this change your picture of God?
Who am I? — Are you often pouring yourself out to love others while seldom pausing to be filled with God's love?
How shall I respond? — How much time will you set aside today to quietly receive God's love?
lessons.jesus: At his baptism Jesus heard the Father say, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.” At that point he had not yet performed a single miracle. All of Jesus' loving service throughout his life flowed out of this assurance: he was loved by the Father.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for loving me first and sending your Son as the atoning sacrifice for my sins. I confess that there is no true love in me; so often it is only bargaining and calculation. Fill me with your love, so that my love flows from you and reaches every person around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: First thing in the morning, pray silently: “I love because God first loved me.”
Write down three pieces of evidence that God has loved you today
For one of my 2s: turn the love you have received from God into a word of encouragement
lessons.noon: “We love him, because he first loved us.” — Lord, right now fill me first, then let it flow out.

lessons.title: What Love Really Is
lessons.theme: Love is not a feeling but the shape of Christ's life

v: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.

lessons.still: Read these four verses slowly. Then replace every “love” with “Jesus” and read them again. Be still for a moment and let the Holy Spirit show you which line touches you most. Linger on that line and tell the Lord what you feel.
teach: People often read 1 Corinthians 13 at weddings, as though it were a romantic poem. But Paul wrote this chapter to a church torn by envy, factions and boasting about spiritual gifts. It was not written for honeymooners but for brothers and sisters in the middle of conflict.

Paul gives fifteen descriptions in one breath: two positive statements to begin, eight “nots”, one “rejoices with the truth”, and then four “all things”. Love is not only a warm feeling; it is concrete actions and choices. You will notice that nearly all eight “nots” deal with the self: love does not brag, is not proud, does not seek its own way, keeps no record of wrongs. The opposite of true love is the self-ruled life.

Try replacing “love” with “Jesus” and every line fits perfectly. Replace it with “I” and you can hardly read on. That is exactly the point: we cannot live out this kind of love by our own strength; only by letting Jesus live in us. The mindset shift: not “I must try hard to achieve these fifteen things,” but “Lord, please become this love in me.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight “nots” in this passage are all portraits of the self-emptied life: not putting ourselves at the centre, not fighting for our own rights, not keeping a record of other people's wrongs. Humility is laying down power and returning to our place, and so is love: we stop acting as judge and return to the place of a servant.
q: Who is God? — When you read the passage with “Jesus” in place of “love”, what kind of Lord do you see?
Who am I? — When you read it with your own name in place of “love”, which line can you hardly get through?
How shall I respond? — In which line will you ask Jesus to live himself out in you today?
lessons.jesus: “Bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things”: this is exactly how Jesus loved Peter. Peter denied the Lord three times, yet after the resurrection Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love me?” He kept no record of wrongs; instead he restored Peter and entrusted him with feeding his sheep.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are what love really is. I confess that my love so often seeks its own way and keeps account of others' wrongs. I cannot do this by myself. Live out in me a love that is patient and kind. Take away the bragging and pride in me, and reign in my heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Copy out 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 once, replacing “love” with “Jesus”
For one of my 2s: today, don't bring up any of their past mistakes
Memorise this week's verse: 1 Corinthians 13:4
lessons.noon: “Love is patient and is kind.” — Lord, right now please become this love in me.

lessons.title: Love Your Enemies
lessons.theme: Only love that reaches our enemies shows it is the Father's love

v: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.

lessons.still: Be still, and honestly allow the face of someone who has hurt you to come to mind. Don't suppress what you feel; tell the Lord exactly how it is. Then do just one thing: speak a simple blessing over that person, even if your heart is still reluctant.
teach: When the sun rises, it doesn't first check whether the people below are good or bad before deciding whether to shine on them. When the rain falls, it doesn't land only on the fields of the righteous. Jesus uses the most everyday scenes of nature to describe a love that is beyond nature: a love given not according to what the other deserves but according to the nature of the one who loves.

“Love your neighbour and hate your enemy” was the common view in Jesus' day. But Jesus said: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven. He doesn't mean we become God's children by loving our enemies; he means children resemble their Father. Loving our enemies is the family likeness, because this is exactly how the Father loved us when we were his enemies.

Loving our enemies does not mean condoning evil or having no boundaries, nor does it mean pretending we were not hurt. It is a choice of direction: not repaying evil for evil, leaving judgement to God, and praying for the other person's good. This is humanly impossible, and precisely because it is impossible, it shows that this fruit comes from the life of Christ and not from our own self-cultivation.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person pays back an eye for an eye and wants to be the judge, which is to take God's place. The self-emptied person leaves vengeance to God and returns to a human being's place. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and is often the only key that unlocks a stalemate.
q: Who is God? — The Father makes his sun rise on the evil and the good. What kind of heart does this show you?
Who am I? — Is there an “enemy” in your heart whom you have secretly been hoping will get what they deserve?
How shall I respond? — What is the first prayer you can pray for that person today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was crucified, he prayed for those who mocked him and nailed him to the cross: “Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.” He not only taught us to love our enemies; he lived it out himself in his moment of deepest agony. And we were among the very enemies he loved.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for loving me while I was still your enemy. I confess there is still resentment in my heart and I want to avenge myself. Today I hand judgement back to you, and I bless the person who hurt me. Let your love in me overcome my bitterness, and make me like a true child of yours. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Speak one specific blessing over someone who has hurt you
Write down what you want to “get even” over, and hand it to God
For one of my 2s: if the relationship is tense, pray for them first instead of arguing
lessons.noon: “And pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you” — Lord, right now I leave vengeance with you and bless them.

lessons.title: The Good Samaritan
lessons.theme: Love doesn't ask “Who is my neighbour?” but goes and becomes a neighbour

v: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

lessons.still: Imagine yourself walking on that road down to Jericho. Ask the Lord to show you who is lying “half dead” by the roadside on your path today. Wait quietly, and let the Holy Spirit lay a person or a need on your heart.
teach: Both the priest and the Levite “saw” him, and passed by on the other side. Perhaps they had good reasons: hurrying to serve at the temple, afraid of becoming ceremonially unclean, worried the robbers might still be around. We too often have good reasons not to stop: too busy, too much trouble, none of my business. Love is often defeated not by evil but by busyness.

The expert in the law asked, “Who is my neighbour?” He wanted to draw a boundary around love. But when Jesus finished the parable, he turned the question around: who became a neighbour to the man? The question moves from “Who deserves my love?” to “Whose neighbour am I willing to become?” The Samaritan saw, was moved with compassion, went to him, bandaged him, lifted him up and cared for him. Love is a chain of costly actions.

Our idea of love needs to shift from drawing lines to crossing them. Your 2s are not only the people who like you; they include the wounded by the roadside, people who may never be able to repay you. You don't need to do anything dramatic today. Just be willing to stop, go one step further, give a little more time, and let Christ's compassion reach someone through you.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks. The priest and the Levite missed the person for the sake of the task; the Samaritan set the task aside and took the person to heart. The self-emptied life no longer asks, “What's in it for me?” but, “Lord, how do you want me to love this person?”
q: Who is God? — Jesus is like the Samaritan who stopped. How have you experienced him stopping for you?
Who am I? — What “good reason” do you most often use to walk past people who are hurting?
How shall I respond? — For whom are you willing to stop and go one step further today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is the true Good Samaritan. We lay by the roadside, beaten half dead by sin, and religion and the law could only pass by. But he came to us himself, was moved with compassion, healed our wounds with his blood, and paid every cost to care for us to the very end.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for stopping for me when I was half dead, for healing me and caring for me. I confess that I often walk past people in need for the sake of busyness and convenience. Give me a heart that is moved with compassion, and let me become a neighbour to someone today. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Today, notice someone who needs help, and stop to greet them
Set aside one “too busy” task and spend that time with someone instead
For one of my 2s: give them some care that costs you something
lessons.noon: “Go and do likewise.” — Lord, right now let me stop and be a neighbour to someone.

lessons.title: Practising Love Toward My 2
lessons.theme: Love not only in word, but in deed and in truth

v: By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?
My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.

lessons.still: Take out last week's “My 2 List”. Pray quietly and ask the Holy Spirit to show you the one person you are to love in a concrete way this week. Write their name on this page, then draw a small cross beside it to remember how the Lord has loved you.
teach: A letter full of “I love you” that never turns into anything will disappoint in the end; a bowl of hot soup quietly brought out late at night can say more than a thousand words. John says: let us not love only in word or with the tongue, but in deed and in truth. The fruit of love is something people can touch and taste.

John defines love from the cross: “By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us.” Then he brings that lofty truth down to the most ordinary place: seeing a brother in need and closing our hearts to him. Laying down our lives for our brothers seldom means actually dying; far more often it means giving up our time, money, pride and convenience.

This week we have looked at the source of love, the shape of love, loving our enemies and being a neighbour. Now choose one of your 2s and plan a concrete act of love: a meal, a letter, a visit, an apology that is long overdue. Love is the root of all the fruit. Next week we will see the second fruit that grows naturally out of love: joy.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your lifestyle changes; change your lifestyle and your relationships change. The fruit of love doesn't come from self-cultivation; it is Christ's self-giving love flowing out through a self-emptied person. Loving one “2” in a concrete way is building God's kingdom system here on earth.
q: Who is God? — The Lord laid down his life for us. How does this redefine what you understand by “love”?
Who am I? — Do you often say kind things to one of your 2s while seldom showing it in action?
How shall I respond? — This week, toward which 2 will you take what concrete act of love?
lessons.jesus: Jesus' love was always concrete: he touched lepers, cooked breakfast for his disciples, and from the cross entrusted his mother to John. Even in his moment of greatest pain he was thinking of other people's needs. His love never stopped at words.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you laid down your life for me, and so I know what love is. Remove the hardness that closes my heart to compassion, so that my love is not only in word and tongue but in deed and in truth. This week I want to love the 2 you have given me. Please love them yourself, through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: complete one concrete act of love this week
For this 2, give up a block of time you had meant to keep for yourself
Write down one moment this week when you experienced the fruit of love
lessons.noon: “Let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only” — Lord, right now let your love become my action.

mem.t: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”

lessons.title: Joy That Doesn't Depend on Circumstances
lessons.theme: Joy is the stillness of deep water, not the spray on the surface

v: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
as sorrowful yet always rejoicing, as poor yet making many rich, as having nothing and yet possessing all things.

lessons.still: Honestly name one thing that is making you unhappy right now. Don't deny it and don't magnify it. Then take a deep breath and say to the Lord, “Lord, this is real, but you are more real.” Quietly let your heart turn from your circumstances to the Lord himself.
teach: The surface of the sea may be whipped up by storms while the depths remain calm. What the world calls “happiness” is mostly spray on the surface: passing an exam, getting a raise or a promotion, children who behave. It rises and falls with circumstances. But the joy the Spirit produces is like a deep ocean current that doesn't change direction because of the wind and waves above.

Paul and Silas had been beaten with rods, thrown into the inner prison and fastened in the stocks. Things could hardly have been worse, yet at midnight they were praying and singing hymns. This was not self-hypnosis; their joy simply wasn't founded inside that prison cell. Paul later described himself as “sorrowful, yet always rejoicing.” Sorrow and joy can exist side by side, because joy is rooted in a deeper place.

Our mindset needs to shift from “I'll be joyful once my circumstances improve” to “The Lord has not changed, so I can rejoice.” Joy is not denying pain, nor forcing a smile; it is seeing the Lord's presence and sovereign rule even in the midst of pain. Our focus is on Jesus, not on our circumstances. This is the first key to the fruit of joy.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Keep your focus on Jesus, not on yourself, not on others, not on circumstances. Live from the heart by the Spirit, and your heart is glad; live from the head by yourself, and you are full of worry. Joy is the life of Christ flowing naturally out of a self-emptied person, not something we cultivate ourselves or that depends on circumstances cooperating.
q: Who is God? — Paul could still sing hymns in prison. What kind of God did he know?
Who am I? — Which circumstances does your happiness mostly depend on?
How shall I respond? — In something that isn't going your way today, how will you turn your focus back to Jesus?
lessons.jesus: On the night he was betrayed, knowing the cross lay just ahead, Jesus still sang a hymn with his disciples before going out to the Mount of Olives. His joy was not built on favourable circumstances but on his relationship with the Father and on the Father's will.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that my heart is often pulled about by circumstances: happy when things go well, discouraged when they don't. Root my joy in you. Even in today's “prison cell” I will pray and sing, because you have not changed. Let your joy be the deep ocean within me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In something that isn't going your way, sing a hymn of praise
Write a sentence in the pattern “as… yet…” to describe your situation
For one of my 2s: share something you are still thankful for in the middle of difficulty
lessons.noon: “As sorrowful yet always rejoicing” — Lord, right now my joy is rooted in you.

lessons.title: Rejoicing in the Lord
lessons.theme: The source of joy is not a thing but a Person: the Lord himself

v: I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”
Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.

lessons.still: Place your hand on your heart and quietly repeat, “The Lord is at hand.” Say it three times, a little more slowly each time. Don't picture the Lord far away; acknowledge that he is right beside you and within you at this very moment. Let his presence be the starting point of your joy today.
teach: A small child can have a wonderful time in a crowded place, not because the crowd is fun, but because he is holding his father's hand. Once he lets go and can't find his father, even the liveliest place will reduce him to tears. Our joy is like that: it doesn't depend on what is around us but on whose hand we are holding.

Paul wrote Philippians from prison, yet he keeps coming back to joy. He says, “Rejoice in the Lord always,” and the key is “in the Lord.” Jesus also said he spoke so that “my joy” may remain in you. The fruit of joy is not an emotion we manufacture; it is the Lord's own joy coming to live in us.

Paul immediately adds, “Let your gentleness be known to all. The Lord is at hand.” People who rejoice in the Lord don't need to compete or grab, because they already have the best. The mindset shift: from “I need to get more before I can be joyful” to “I already have the Lord, so I rejoice.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person finds joy in getting, so there is never enough; the self-emptied person finds joy in the Lord, so they are always content. A gentle, yielding heart is a mark of the self-emptied life, and the self-emptied life is the soil in which joy grows. Let Jesus reign, and the heart finds rest.
q: Who is God? — Jesus wants to give you “my joy”. What kind of joy is his?
Who am I? — Has your recent joy been “in the Lord” or “in things”?
How shall I respond? — How will you practise an awareness that “the Lord is at hand” today?
lessons.jesus: When the seventy disciples came back from their mission, they were overjoyed that even demons submitted to them. But Jesus said, “Don't rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” He brought their joy back from the results of ministry to their relationship with God.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for giving me your joy. I confess that I often think I'll be happy only when I have more. Today I will rejoice in you always, because you are near. Give me a gentle and yielding heart that doesn't compete or grab, but takes you alone as my greatest joy. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Three times today, pray silently: “The Lord is at hand.”
Let go of something you were trying to get, and show a yielding spirit
For one of my 2s: tell them something the Lord has given you joy about
lessons.noon: “Rejoice in the Lord always!” — Lord, right now I hold your hand tightly.

lessons.title: Habakkuk's Joy
lessons.theme: Joy even with nothing left, because God is still my God

v: For even though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines, the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food, the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls,
yet I will rejoice in the LORD. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!

lessons.still: List a few things in your life that are not bearing fruit right now, and lay them one by one before the Lord. Then slowly say that one word: “Yet…” Pause, and wait for the Holy Spirit to help you finish the sentence.
teach: The six things Habakkuk lists were everything an agricultural society of his day depended on to survive: figs, wine, olive oil, grain, flocks and herds. In today's terms: the income is gone, the savings are gone, the job is gone, and even health is gone. When everything is lost, what is left?

The book of Habakkuk opens with a string of complaints: “Yahweh, how long will I cry, and you will not hear?” By the end, his circumstances have not changed; what has changed is Habakkuk's perspective. He moves from questioning God to waiting on God, and finally declares, “Yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.” That little word “yet” is the most beautiful turning point of faith.

This joy is not naive optimism; it is faith refined through struggle. The shift in perspective is from earthly to heavenly, from temporary to eternal. When everything else can be lost, the “God of my salvation” cannot. If the root of our joy is in God, no circumstance can pull it up.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Shift your perspective: from the human to God's, from earthly to heavenly, from temporary to eternal. Change your mindset and your life changes. Habakkuk's joy did not come from self-cultivation; he moved his roots from circumstances to God. The self-emptied person may lose everything and still have the infinite God.
q: Who is God? — Habakkuk moved from complaint to rejoicing. How did his knowledge of God change?
Who am I? — Where in your life is “the fig tree not flourishing”?
How shall I respond? — Are you willing to speak your own “yet” today?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus was stripped of everything: his clothes, his friends, his reputation, even the felt presence of the Father. Yet at the end he said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.” With nothing left, he still entrusted himself completely to the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, I lay before you every fruitless place in my life. I confess that I often grieve over what I have lost and complain when things go wrong. Yet I will rejoice in you; I will be joyful in the God of my salvation. Even if everything changes, you never change. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write your own “Though… yet…” prayer
About something you have lost, say to the Lord, “Yet I will still rejoice”
For one of my 2s: walk alongside someone who is going through a low valley
lessons.noon: “Yet I will rejoice in the LORD.” — Lord, right now I choose to rejoice in you.

lessons.title: Joy Is Strength
lessons.theme: The joy of the Lord is my strength to keep going

v: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.

lessons.still: Think of the area of your life where you are most worn out. Don't ask for strength first; ask first for the Lord's presence: “Lord, in your presence is fullness of joy.” Stay quietly before him. Let joy return first, and strength will follow.
teach: When a car runs out of fuel, you can't push it very far; fill the tank, and it runs on its own. Many of us, when we are exhausted, try to push ourselves further by willpower, and the more we push, the more tired we get. Nehemiah says the joy of the Lord is your strength. Joy is not a prize awarded after our strength is used up; it is the source of our strength.

When the returned exiles heard the Book of the Law, they realised how far they had strayed from God, and they wept. But Nehemiah told them: today is holy; do not grieve. He was not telling them to take sin lightly; he was telling them, having confessed, to lift their eyes and see God's grace. The psalm also says, “In your presence is fullness of joy.” Our tank of joy is filled up in God's presence.

So practising joy does not start with doing more things; it starts with returning to God's presence. Nehemiah also said, “Send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared.” Real joy always overflows and becomes a feast shared with others. The mindset shift: joy is not the reward after the work is done; it is the fuel to begin serving.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The path of service begins with the Spirit: Spirit (the Holy Spirit's guidance) comes first, then Understanding (Scripture), Life (the life of Jesus), Service (letting Jesus reign) and God (all glory to him). The strength of joy does not come from our own willpower but from God's presence. The self-emptied person no longer pushes the car by their own strength, but lets the Holy Spirit fill the tank, and joy becomes the driving force of service.
q: Who is God? — “In your presence is fullness of joy.” When have you experienced being satisfied in God's presence?
Who am I? — Do you often grit your teeth and push on by willpower, neglecting to fill up in the Lord's presence first?
How shall I respond? — How will you come back to God's presence first today, before facing your work?
lessons.jesus: Hebrews tells us that Jesus, “for the joy that was set before him, endured the cross, despising its shame.” Joy became his strength to walk to the cross; he saw the Father's will being accomplished and the day of our redemption.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often push on in my own strength and grow more and more tired. Today I come back into your presence. Fill me with your joy and let it be my strength. I don't want to rejoice only for myself; let my joy overflow and be shared with those in need. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before starting your work, spend five quiet minutes in the Lord's presence
Share something good with someone who is in need
For one of my 2s: invite them for a meal and share your joy
lessons.noon: “For the joy of the LORD is your strength.” — Lord, right now please fill my tank.

lessons.title: Sharing Joy with My 2
lessons.theme: Joy shared is never diminished; it only multiplies

v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
Always rejoice.
Pray without ceasing.
In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.

lessons.still: Open your “My 2 List”. Quietly thank God once for each name, naming one thing you are grateful for because of that person. Then ask the Holy Spirit to show you which 2 you are to share joy with this week, or weep with.
teach: When one candle lights another, its own flame doesn't grow dimmer, but the room grows brighter. Joy is like that: when shared it is not diminished; it multiplies. In Jesus' parables, the shepherd who finds his sheep and the woman who finds her coin both do the same thing: they call their friends and neighbours to “rejoice with me”.

Paul says, “Rejoice with those who rejoice.” It sounds simple, but it isn't easy: when others are happy, the self-ruled heart tends toward envy and comparison. “Weep with those who weep” asks us to set aside the urge to explain and lecture, and simply be with people. Both require the self-emptied life. 1 Thessalonians 5 links rejoicing always, praying continually and giving thanks in everything; the three nourish one another.

This week we have seen that joy does not depend on circumstances but is found in the Lord; that even at the end of our resources we can still say “yet”; and that joy is strength. Now share joy in a concrete way with one of your 2s. Love is the root, joy is the blossom; with joy in place, next week we will learn a deeper fruit for our life with others: peace.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride provokes pride, and envy steals joy; humility inspires humility, and rejoicing together multiplies joy. Giving thanks in everything means letting Jesus receive all the glory. Joy is not self-cultivation; it is the life of Christ flowing out of a self-emptied person, and from them on to others.
q: Who is God? — In Christ, God's will for you is to “always rejoice”. What does this show you of his heart?
Who am I? — When things go better for someone else than for you, can you truly rejoice with them?
How shall I respond? — This week, which 2 will you share joy with, or weep alongside?
lessons.jesus: At the wedding in Cana, Jesus turned water into wine; his first miracle protected the joy of a wedding feast. He also wept at the tomb of Lazarus. He rejoiced with those who rejoiced and wept with those who wept, entering fully into people's lives.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for giving me joy. Take away the envy and comparison in me, so that I can truly rejoice with those who rejoice and quietly weep with those who weep. This week, use me to bring your joy to one of my 2s. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: this week, share one way God has been gracious to you
Sincerely congratulate someone who is doing better than you
Tonight, write down three things you are thankful for
lessons.noon: “Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks.” — Lord, right now let my joy light up someone else.

mem.t: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.

lessons.title: Reconciled to God
lessons.theme: All peace begins with being reconciled to God

v: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

lessons.still: Be still and imagine yourself standing before the cross. Lay down there, one by one, your past failures and any unresolved guilt. Hear the Lord say to you, “I have reconciled you to God.” Take a deep breath and let this peace settle into the depths of your heart.
teach: If a pond's source is polluted, no amount of cleaning downstream will make the water clear. Conflict between people often stems from conflict between people and God. When we are cut off from God, there is an unspeakable unrest inside us, and that unrest turns into defensiveness, comparison and attack, eventually flowing into every relationship.

Paul says, “Being justified by faith, we have peace with God.” This peace is not a ceasefire we negotiated; it is a reconciliation God himself accomplished in Christ: “All things are of God,” who does “not reckon their trespasses to them.” The cross is the bridge of reconciliation between heaven and earth; enemies become children.

Even more wonderful, God has entrusted us with “the ministry of reconciliation.” We first receive peace, and then we can pass peace on. The mindset shift: peace does not begin with “I've sorted things out with that person,” but with “I have been reconciled to God.” Once the source is clear, the relationships downstream can become clear too.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships: first with God, then with ourselves, then with others, then with tasks. The fruit of peace is not a matter of managing our emotions by self-cultivation; once we are reconciled to God, the life of Christ flows naturally out of a self-emptied person. All things are from God, and all glory goes to God.
q: Who is God? — “All things are of God.” God took the initiative to reconcile you to himself. What kind of God does this show you?
Who am I? — Is there still some unresolved unrest between you and God?
How shall I respond? — How will you bring your reconciliation with God into one relationship today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “made peace through the blood of his cross” (Colossians 1:20). He was not a third party mediating from the middle; he took the brokenness of both sides upon himself and paid the price of reconciliation with his own body.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for reconciling me to yourself in Christ and not counting my trespasses against me. I lay all my guilt and unrest at the foot of the cross. Let your peace begin in my relationship with you and flow into my family, my workplace and my church, and make me a messenger of reconciliation. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Confess to the Lord one thing that still troubles you, and receive his forgiveness
Write “I have been reconciled to God” and put it up by your desk
For one of my 2s: share how you have experienced being reconciled to God
lessons.noon: “We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” — Lord, right now I find rest in you.

lessons.title: Peace Beyond Understanding
lessons.theme: Peace is not the absence of storms but the Lord's presence in the storm

v: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

lessons.still: Name the things that are worrying you, one at a time. With each one, open your hands as though handing it over. Finish with a word of thanks: “Lord, thank you for hearing.” Then quietly let peace stand guard at the door of your heart.
teach: Picture a painting: beside a waterfall in a raging storm, with the wind howling and spray flying, a little bird sits safely in its nest in a crevice of the rock. Peace is not the absence of the storm; it is a secure place within the storm. The peace the world offers is “the problem is solved”; the peace the Lord gives is “I am with you.”

Paul gives a concrete path: don't be anxious about anything, pray about everything, and do it with thanksgiving. The result is that God's peace will “guard” your hearts and minds. “Guard” is a military term, like soldiers garrisoning a city. Jesus said, “Not as the world gives do I give to you.” The world's peace depends on conditions; the Lord's peace depends on his presence, which is why it “surpasses all understanding”.

The fruit of peace must first grow in our own hearts before we can bring it into our relationships. An anxious heart easily infects others with anxiety; only a guarded heart can become a quiet strength in someone else's storm. The mindset shift: from “I'll have peace once I have everything under control” to “I have peace when I hand things over to God.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: Worry is often another form of the self-ruled life: I want control, I want to guarantee the outcome, which amounts to sitting on God's throne. Handing our worries to God is laying down power and returning to our place: let people be people and let God be God. Live from the heart by the Spirit, and your heart is glad; live from the head by yourself, and you are full of worry.
q: Who is God? — “My peace I give to you.” How is Jesus' peace different from the world's peace?
Who am I? — What have you been trying to control yourself, and lost your peace over?
How shall I respond? — How will you practise “prayer plus thanksgiving” to deal with worry today?
lessons.jesus: When a fierce storm arose, Jesus was asleep in the stern on a cushion. The terrified disciples woke him; he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm. The peace in his heart came before the calm on the water, and today he is in our boat too.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I hand my worries to you one by one, and I thank you for hearing me. I confess that I often want to control everything myself. Let your peace, which surpasses all understanding, guard my heart and mind, so that I can bring peace to others in their storms. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three worries, and pray through each one with thanksgiving
When you want to control the outcome today, pray silently: “Let God be God.”
For one of my 2s: when they are anxious, quietly pray with them
lessons.noon: “And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.” — Lord, right now I hand my worries to you.

lessons.title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
lessons.theme: The Lord wants me not only to enjoy peace but to make peace

v: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

lessons.still: Think of a relationship around you that is tense right now: within your family, among colleagues, in your small group. Don't rush to find a solution. First quietly bless both sides, and ask the Lord to give you the wisdom that comes from above.
teach: Some people are like matches: wherever they go, fires break out. Others are like fire extinguishers: wherever they go, things cool down. Jesus did not say “Blessed are the peace-lovers” but “Blessed are the peacemakers.” It is not just avoiding conflict and keeping ourselves clean; it is stepping into the brokenness and becoming someone who mends.

Jesus said peacemakers “shall be called children of God”, because God himself is the greatest peacemaker of all, reconciling the world to himself in Christ. James points out that the wisdom from above is “first pure, then peaceful.” True peace is not papering over the cracks or covering up right and wrong; it has purity as its foundation and mercy as its attitude.

James adds, “The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.” Here is another fruit image: peace is like a seed that must be sown and waited on before it grows into the fruit of righteousness. The mindset shift: I don't have to force both sides to reconcile immediately, but I can sow seeds of peace in every conversation.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Making peace requires the self-emptied life: not rushing to prove that we are right, not taking sides, not stirring things up. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility, and both sides win. Peacemakers are the very people who build God's kingdom system on earth, letting God's kingdom come between people.
q: Who is God? — God is called the God of peace. How is he doing his peacemaking work in you?
Who am I? — In conflict, are you more like a match or a fire extinguisher?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship can you sow a seed of peace today?
lessons.jesus: Among Jesus' disciples were Matthew, who had collected taxes for Rome, and Simon the Zealot, who had resisted Rome. In the world they were sworn enemies, yet beside Jesus they became brothers. Jesus is the Prince of Peace who breaks down the dividing wall of hostility.
lessons.pray: Lord of peace, make me a peacemaker, not someone who starts fires. Give me the wisdom from above that is first pure, then peaceful and full of mercy. Today, in the relationships where you have placed me, use me to sow seeds of peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Today, don't repeat a single remark that could cause misunderstanding
In a tense situation, say one thing that calms things down
For one of my 2s: if they are at odds with someone, pray with them
lessons.noon: “Blessed are the peacemakers.” — Lord, right now make me an instrument of your peace.

lessons.title: Children of Peace in the Midst of Conflict
lessons.theme: Conflict is not failure but a place where the fruit of peace can grow

v: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
“If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

lessons.still: Ask the Holy Spirit to remind you: is there someone who “has something against you”? Don't argue over who was right or wrong; just honestly admit that there is a crack in this relationship. Gently speak that person's name and place them before the Lord.
teach: When a garment gets a small hole, a few stitches will mend it if you deal with it promptly; leave it, and the tear only grows. Relationships are the same. We often think, “I'll deal with it once I've calmed down,” or “Time heals everything.” But time does not automatically mend a rift; often it only lets the wound harden into a scar.

Jesus says something startling: if you are offering your gift at the altar and remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there and go and be reconciled first. Notice: it is your brother who has something against you, not you against him. The initiative lies with me. Paul says, “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you”: I cannot control the other person's response, but I can take responsibility for my own part.

The hardest thing in conflict is letting go of “I am right.” Children of peace do not ignore right and wrong; they are willing to deal with their own part first: admitting their own faults, speaking the truth in love, and not repaying evil for evil. The mindset shift: conflict is not the end of a relationship but the building site where the Holy Spirit grows the fruit of peace.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is leaving our place and grasping power; in conflict, “I have to win” is grasping power. Humility is laying down power and returning to our place. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than things: better to lose the argument than to lose a brother.
q: Who is God? — God values reconciliation even above sacrifice. What does this say about what matters to him?
Who am I? — Are you waiting for the other person to apologise first before you are willing to make peace?
How shall I respond? — For which rift will you take the first step today?
lessons.jesus: On the night he was betrayed, Peter drew his sword and cut off the ear of the high priest's servant, but Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him. In the most heated conflict, Jesus did not repay evil for evil; instead he healed a man from the enemy's side.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often wait for others to apologise first, and I often want to win in conflict. Give me the courage to go and be reconciled first, and to do all I can to live at peace with everyone. In conflict, help me let go of “I am right” and let you reign. Heal the rifts between me and others. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: take the initiative and send a message of reconciliation about a rift
In a disagreement today, say first, “I was in the wrong too”
Write down your most common reaction in conflict, and hand it to the Lord
lessons.noon: “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.” — Lord, right now I am willing to take the first step toward peace.

lessons.title: Making Peace with My 2
lessons.theme: Let the peace of Christ rule in your heart and work in your relationships

v: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,

lessons.still: Open your “My 2 List” and ask the Holy Spirit to show you which relationship most needs peace. Quietly bless that person, and ask the Lord to show you one small thing you can do for this relationship this week.
teach: In a ball game, when the referee blows the whistle, play stops and every player has to listen. Paul says, “Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts,” and the word for “rule” originally carried the sense of acting as umpire. When I am with my 2, I must let the peace of Christ blow the whistle in my heart, rather than letting anger, hurt feelings or pride make the call.

Hebrews says, “Pursue peace with all people, and holiness,” setting peace and holiness side by side. “Pursue” is an active word, like a hunter chasing his quarry. Peace does not arrive by itself; we have to pursue it actively. And true peace is bound up with holiness: it does not compromise the truth but receives one another within the truth.

This week we have walked through being reconciled to God, peace in our hearts, making peace, and reconciliation in the midst of conflict. Now we are to make peace concretely with one of our 2s. But peace often takes time; people don't change overnight. Next week we will learn a fruit closely tied to peace: patience.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God's kingdom system is fulfilling the Lord's Prayer: your kingdom come, your will be done on earth. Peace at home, at work and in the church is what the kingdom of heaven looks like on earth. Peace is not a matter of cultivating a better temper by our own effort; it is letting the peace of Christ rule in a self-emptied heart.
q: Who is God? — The peace of Christ is willing to “umpire” in your heart. What comfort does this bring you?
Who am I? — When you face your 2, who usually blows the whistle in your heart: peace, anger or pride?
How shall I respond? — This week, what one thing will you do to make peace with which 2?
lessons.jesus: When the risen Jesus first appeared to his disciples, his very first words were, “Peace be to you!” These were the disciples who had scattered and fled when he needed them most, yet he spoke not one word of reproach. He gave them peace first and restored the broken relationship.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, let your peace rule in my heart. When anger and hurt want to make the call, blow the whistle of peace. This week I want to make peace with one of my 2s; give me wisdom and courage, and a thankful heart. May your kingdom come in our relationships. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: take one concrete peacemaking action this week
When you feel anger rising today, pray silently: “Let the peace of Christ rule.”
Before bed, pray with a thankful heart for each of today's relationships
lessons.noon: “And let the peace of God rule in your hearts” — Lord, right now blow the whistle of peace in my heart.

mem.t: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

lessons.title: God's Long-Suffering Patience
lessons.theme: I can be patient because God has first been patient with me

v: The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

lessons.still: Think back over how long God has waited for you, before and since you came to faith: how many times you went astray and he did not give up on you; how many times you fell into the same sin and he still welcomed you back. Quietly count up this patience, and say to the Lord, “Thank you for not giving up on me.”
teach: You may have watched a potter at the wheel. When the clay goes lopsided, the potter doesn't throw it away; he presses it with both hands, lets the wheel turn again, presses again, over and over. We often feel that God is “too slow” with our growth, but we rarely stop to think that God's patience with us is far longer than our patience with anyone.

The Israelites had just made the golden calf, yet God proclaimed his name before Moses: “slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.” The Hebrew for “slow to anger” literally means “long of nose”: anger has a long way to travel before it comes out. Peter likewise says that what looks like the Lord's delay is in fact his patience, not wanting anyone to perish.

The word for “patience” among the fruit of the Spirit literally means “long-tempered” or “long-hearted”, and it mainly refers to patience with people. We lack patience with others often because we have forgotten how patient God has been with us. The mindset shift: from “Why hasn't he changed yet?” to “God has waited for me like this, again and again.” Only those who have been shown patience can learn to be patient with others.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fruit of patience does not come from gritting our teeth and cultivating it ourselves; it is God's long-suffering life flowing into a self-emptied person. The self-ruled person demands that others keep to their timetable; the self-emptied person hands the timetable back to God and lets God be God.
q: Who is God? — Right after the golden calf, God proclaimed himself “slow to anger”. What kind of God does this show you?
Who am I? — What made you lose your patience most recently?
How shall I respond? — How will you remember God's patience with you today and extend it to others?
lessons.jesus: Peter denied the Lord three times, and Jesus did not give up on him; Thomas doubted, and Jesus appeared to him again. He bore patiently with his disciples' slowness again and again, and even after his resurrection he was still patiently explaining the Scriptures to them. Jesus is the living picture of the Father's long-suffering patience.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for your long patience with me, and for never giving up on me each time I strayed. I confess that I am often impatient with people and expect them to keep to my timetable. Put your patient heart within me, so that I wait for the people around me the way you have waited for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three ways God has been patient with you
When you feel like hurrying someone along today, first pray silently: “God waits for me like this too.”
For one of my 2s: let go of one thing you keep pushing them to change
lessons.noon: “A merciful and gracious God, slow to anger” — Lord, right now let me be slow to anger, as you are.

lessons.title: The Endurance of Job
lessons.theme: Endurance doesn't mean never asking why, but asking without leaving God

v: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

lessons.still: Honestly name one suffering you have never understood, and tell God your “Why?” directly, without dressing it up. Then be silent for a while and say, “Lord, I don't understand, but I will not leave you.”
teach: A patient on the operating table may not understand why the surgeon has to cut him open, but he trusts the surgeon's hands. Job's situation was harder still: he had no idea what was happening in heaven; he only knew that in a single day he had lost his children and his wealth, and later his health as well. Endurance often means trusting those hands even when we cannot see the whole picture.

Many people think Job's endurance meant suffering in silence. In fact, most of the book of Job is his struggling, lamenting and questioning. But he always brought his questions to God, rather than turning his back on God. James says, “You have heard of the perseverance of Job, and have seen the Lord in the outcome.” The end that those who endure come to see is a Lord full of compassion and mercy.

The word for endurance here literally means “to remain standing under a heavy load.” It is the other side of the same life as long-suffering patience with people: standing firm in our circumstances, and making room for others in our relationships. The mindset shift: endurance is not suppressing our emotions; it is bringing our real emotions to God, and then choosing to stay.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Job's words, “Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away,” are a declaration of the self-emptied life: nothing was ever mine in the first place; it all belongs to God. When we neither cling nor try to be in charge, we can still bless God's name in loss. Endurance is the overflow of Christ's life, not the product of self-cultivation.
q: Who is God? — Job blessed God's name even after losing everything. What kind of God did he know?
Who am I? — Do you bring your “why” to God, or take it away from God?
How shall I respond? — In what way will you choose to stay with God today, even when you don't understand?
lessons.jesus: In Gethsemane, Jesus was sorrowful to the point of death. Three times he asked the Father to take the cup away, yet each time he said, “Not my will, but yours be done.” He truly struggled, yet he did not walk away from the Father's will. This is the perfect picture of endurance.
lessons.pray: Lord, I bring the “why” in my heart to you. I don't understand, but I choose not to leave you. You gave, and you have taken away; blessed be your name. Help me stand firm under the weight, and to see the outcome of your great compassion and mercy. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write God a letter and honestly tell him one “why”
Read Job 42 and notice the outcome God gave Job
For one of my 2s: be with someone who is suffering; say less, listen more
lessons.noon: “The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away.” — Lord, right now, even without understanding, I bless you.

lessons.title: Waiting for God's Time
lessons.theme: Like a farmer, waiting for the season God has set

v: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.
You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

lessons.still: Think of a prayer you have been waiting on for a long time that has not yet been answered. Hand it over to God again. Then be still for a minute, asking for nothing, simply “waiting”, like a farmer looking over his field, trusting that the seed is sprouting in the soil.
teach: No farmer digs up the seed the day after sowing to check whether it has grown. He waters, weeds and waits, trusting that while he cannot see it, life is at work in the soil. Fruit has its season and cannot be forced; fruit ripened too early may look good on the outside but is still raw inside.

James uses the image of a farmer waiting for the early and late rains: the autumn rain makes the seed sprout, the spring rain fills out the grain, and neither rain is under the farmer's control. Isaiah says, “Those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength.” Waiting here is not passively sitting around; the word suggests strands twisted together into a rope, binding ourselves tightly to God and drawing strength from him.

Times of waiting are when God does his deepest work in us. The same is true with people: you have prayed for your 2 for a long time, and they don't seem to have changed. The mindset shift: God's timing is not my timing; my job is to sow and water, and God's is to make it grow. The fruit of patience ripens in the waiting.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person wants to control the clock and see results immediately; the self-emptied person acknowledges that our times are in God's hands. Handing our timetable to God is letting Jesus reign. Shift your perspective from the temporary to the eternal: the coming of the Lord is near, and today's waiting will not be in vain.
q: Who is God? — God does not work according to our timetable. What does this show you of his wisdom?
Who am I? — Do you often want to “dig up the seed” to see whether it has grown?
How shall I respond? — In your waiting, how will you “draw strength from God” today?
lessons.jesus: For thirty years Jesus lived in obscurity as a carpenter in Nazareth, until the time the Father had set for him to begin preaching. Even when his own mother urged him at Cana, he said, “My hour has not yet come.” He submitted completely to the Father's timing.
lessons.pray: Lord, once again I hand over to you the prayer I have waited on for so long. I confess that I often want to force the fruit to ripen and to control the timing. Make me patient like a farmer as I wait, trusting that you are at work where I cannot see. Renew my strength as I wait. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one prayer you are still waiting on, and date it today
When you are stuck in a queue or in traffic today, practise quiet prayer
For one of my 2s: keep praying for them without pushing them to change
lessons.noon: “But those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength.” — Lord, right now, as I wait, I hold tightly to you.

lessons.title: Bearing with Others' Weaknesses
lessons.theme: Bearing with one another in love, carrying others' weaknesses

v: with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
