teach: One tiny match can burn down a whole forest. James says the tongue is like that: the smallest member of the body, yet it boasts great things and sets great fires. A cutting remark may be remembered for a lifetime; an unchecked piece of hearsay can destroy someone’s reputation.

James says, “Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body also.” The tongue is like the bridle of the whole body; rein in the tongue and you rein in the whole person. The psalmist knew he could not control it himself, so he prayed, “Set a watch, Yahweh, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.” That is the secret of self-control — asking God to post a guard at the door of my mouth.

Self-control of the tongue includes: no lying, no judging, no gossip, no complaining, no hurtful jokes. In the internet age it also includes self-control of the fingers — the messages and comments we send. A change of mindset: before you speak, ask three questions: Is it true? Is it helpful? Is it spoken in love?
lessons.light: 321 Light: Everything we do flows from the heart, and the words of our mouth come from the heart too. Self-ruled people use words to raise themselves up and push others down; people living the self-emptied life use words to build others up. Letting Jesus reign begins with letting him reign over my tongue.
q: Who is God? — God created all things by his word — how highly does he value our words?
Who am I? — Where do your words most often slip: complaining, judging, exaggerating, or gossip?
How shall I respond? — Which three questions will you use today to guard your mouth?
lessons.jesus: People marvelled at the gracious words that came from Jesus’ mouth. He spoke with authority, and he also knew when to be silent: faced with trick questions, he answered with wisdom; faced with false accusations, he said nothing. He also warned, “Every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.”
lessons.pray: Lord, set a watch before my mouth; keep the door of my lips. I confess that my tongue often runs out of control and I say many things I should not. Holy Spirit, govern my heart, so that everything that comes out of my mouth builds others up and carries grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Go a whole day without a single word of complaint
Before sending any message or comment, ask the three questions and only then press send
With one of “my 2,” replace one word of criticism with a word that builds up
lessons.noon: “Set a watch, LORD, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.” — Lord, right now guard my mouth.

lessons.title: Self-Control over Desires
lessons.theme: Grace teaches us to live soberly in this present age

v: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;

lessons.still: Honestly name one desire that has been tugging at you lately: eating, buying, watching, scrolling, being affirmed… Don’t be ashamed; lay it out before the Lord and say, “Lord, you are better than this.”
teach: In ancient times, a city without walls was open to enemies at any moment, and thieves could come and go as they pleased. Solomon said, “Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.” A person without self-control lets desires, emotions, advertising and trends come and go in their heart, until they are hollowed out.

What teaches us self-control? Paul’s answer is not the law but grace: “For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men, instructing us… denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age.” To live “soberly” is self-control. Grace does not only forgive us; it also trains us.

Desire itself is not sin; God made us with hunger and longing. The problem comes when desire takes the throne and replaces God. A change of mindset: self-control does not overcome desire merely by “forbidding”; it overcomes by “a greater satisfaction” — when the heart is filled with Christ, secondary things return to their secondary place.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-ruled people centre on satisfying themselves and end up enslaved by their desires; people living the self-emptied life centre on Christ and find true freedom. Change your mindset and you change your life; change your life and you change your lifestyle — self-control is a lifestyle changed by grace.
q: Who is God? — Grace not only forgives you but also “instructs” you — how does that shape the way you see God’s grace?
Who am I? — Which wall of your heart’s city most needs repairing?
How shall I respond? — In which desire will you let Christ’s satisfaction take its place today?
lessons.jesus: The Samaritan woman had spent her whole life searching for satisfaction. At the well Jesus said to her, “Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again.” He did not begin by rebuking her longing; he offered her something better. Only Christ can satisfy the deepest thirst of the human heart.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often let my desires sit on the throne. Thank you that your grace not only forgives me but also teaches me to live soberly in this present age. Fill my heart with yourself, so that I am satisfied in you and no longer led around by my desires. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one desire and deliberately refrain from it once today, replacing it with prayer
Put off an impulse purchase for twenty-four hours before deciding
Take time you would normally spend scrolling on your phone and give it to one of “my 2” with your full attention
lessons.noon: “Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.” — Lord, right now be the wall around the city of my heart.

lessons.title: Self-Control for My 2
lessons.theme: Gladly laying down my own rights to build others up

v: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.
Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, to be building him up.

lessons.still: Think of one of your 2. Quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, which things that I am ‘allowed to do’ don’t actually build them up?” Wait for the Holy Spirit’s prompting, without rushing to defend yourself.
teach: A driver has the right to drive right up to the speed limit, but with an elderly passenger who gets carsick, someone who loves them will naturally slow down. This week we have seen that self-control is the Spirit in charge (Day 1), Paul disciplining his body (Day 2), self-control of the tongue (Day 3), and self-control over desires (Day 4). Today, self-control steps into our relationships.

Paul says, “‘All things are lawful for me,’ but not all things are profitable. ‘All things are lawful for me,’ but not all things build up.” Self-ruled people ask, “Do I have the right?” People living the self-emptied life ask, “Is this good for others?” “Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.” Self-control is not only for my own good; even more, it is for love of others.

Self-control for my 2 might mean voicing one less opinion, spending a little less time on my phone, insisting a little less on my own way. This brings our practice of the nine fruits to a close. Next week we enter “Forgiveness and Restoring Relationships” — the truest test of the nine fruits, in relationships that are broken.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The practice of 920 has reached the ninth fruit. Self-control is letting the Holy Spirit reign, and also putting others’ good ahead of my own rights. For Jesus, for others, not for myself — this is self-denial, and it is the way of life that builds what belongs to God.
q: Who is God? — “Even Christ didn’t please himself” (Romans 15:3) — what does that show you about God?
Who am I? — Do you often defend yourself with “I have the right”?
How shall I respond? — For the good of one of your 2, which right will you lay down today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus had the authority to ask the Father for more than twelve legions of angels, yet he chose not to; he had the right to be served, yet he chose to serve. He said, “The Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve.” His greatest self-control was exercised for our good.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, for my sake you laid down your rights in heaven. Make me willing to lay down my own rights for my 2, not seeking my own good but the good of others. Holy Spirit, reign in my relationships, so that my self-control becomes an expression of love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Let go of one “I have the right” insistence for one of “my 2”
When you are with your family today, leave your phone in another room
Tomorrow (Saturday), review with your spiritual companion: which of the nine fruits do you most need?
lessons.noon: “Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.” — Lord, right now I live for the good of others.

mem.t: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.

lessons.title: Joseph Forgives His Brothers
lessons.theme: Only when we see God’s hand can we let go of people’s wrongs

v: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?
As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive, as is happening today.
Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

lessons.still: Think of someone who once hurt you deeply. Don’t rush to forgive; first tell the Lord honestly about the pain. Then ask him to open your eyes to see, behind it all, his hand that has never once let go of you.
teach: The back of a tapestry is a chaotic mess of tangled threads; turn it over, and there is a beautiful picture. Joseph was sold into Egypt by his brothers, thrown into prison on a false charge, and forgotten for years. From the back, it was a tangle of threads. But years later he told his brothers, “You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.”

Notice Joseph’s first words: “Am I in the place of God?” This is the key to forgiveness. Revenge means climbing onto the judgment seat myself and punishing others in God’s place; forgiveness means stepping down from that seat and returning to my place as a human being. Joseph not only refused revenge; he said, “I will provide for you,” and he “comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.”

Joseph did not deny his brothers’ evil — “you meant evil against me,” he said plainly. Forgiveness does not say, “It was nothing.” It says, “It was something, but I hand it over to God.” This week we learn forgiveness and the restoring of relationships — the deepest test of the nine fruits, in relationships that are broken.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. Unforgiveness is really an expression of the self-ruled life — I want to sit in God’s place and judge. People living the self-emptied life return to their place, and so they can forgive. Humility overcomes pride: Joseph’s forgiveness ended years of hatred among the brothers and saved many lives.
q: Who is God? — “God meant it for good” — in which painful experience have you seen God’s hand?
Who am I? — Are you still sitting on the judgment seat over someone?
How shall I respond? — Are you willing to say to the Lord, “Am I in your place?”
lessons.jesus: Joseph is a foreshadowing of Jesus: betrayed by his brothers, falsely accused, made to suffer, and finally exalted — becoming the saviour of those who betrayed him. Jesus was rejected by his own people and nailed to a cross, yet he became their Saviour, and he prayed, “Father, forgive them.”
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess there are wounds I am still clutching tightly and people I am still judging in my heart. Today I step down from the judgment seat — am I in your place? Help me to see your hand, and give me a forgiving heart, so that I can even speak kindly and bring comfort to those who hurt me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the name of someone you have not yet forgiven, and hand them over to God in prayer
Memorise this week’s verse: Colossians 3:13
If one of “my 2” has hurt you, pray a prayer of blessing over them today
lessons.noon: “You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good” — Lord, right now I trust that your hand is in control.

lessons.title: Seventy Times Seven
lessons.theme: Forgiveness is not a calculation but the way of life of those who have received grace

v: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”
Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

lessons.still: Quietly recall how many times the Lord has forgiven you. The same sins, the same weaknesses — you have come back to him again and again, and he has never once said, “That’s enough.” Let this grace slowly soak into your heart.
teach: Peter thought he was being very generous: “Until seven times?” Seven is the number of completeness. But Jesus said, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.” He did not mean that on the four hundred and ninety-first time we may stop forgiving; he meant that forgiveness is not something to count at all.

Then Jesus told a parable. A servant owed his master ten thousand talents, and the master cancelled the whole debt. But the servant went out, seized a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii by the throat, and refused to show him mercy. The master said, “Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?” The root of the problem was this: he had forgotten how much he had been forgiven.

We refuse to forgive because we make others’ debts too big and our own too small. A change of mindset: I am someone who has been forgiven ten thousand talents. When I remember the grace of the cross, forgiving someone else’s hundred denarii is no longer a heavy command but the natural overflow of gratitude.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and you change your life. Self-ruled people keep accounts of what others owe them; people living the self-emptied life keep count of grace — what God has forgiven them. Forgiveness does not come from self-improvement; it is the life of Christ flowing naturally from those who live the self-emptied life.
q: Who is God? — The master cancelled ten thousand talents — what does that show you about God’s heart?
Who am I? — Whose account are you still keeping in your heart?
How shall I respond? — How will you remember every day the grace of being forgiven?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not only teach forgiveness; he himself is the Master who cancelled our debt of ten thousand talents. On the cross he paid our debt in full, and he welcomes those who turn back to him again and again. It is precisely because he forgave us first that we have the strength to forgive others.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for cancelling my debt of ten thousand talents and forgiving me again and again. Forgive me for so often remembering others’ hundred denarii while forgetting the grace you have given me. Today I choose to stop keeping accounts, and to have mercy on my fellow servants as you have had mercy on me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three things God has forgiven you for, and give thanks for them
Hand over to the Lord an offence you keep replaying in your mind, and stop replaying it
Forgive one of “my 2” for a small thing, and never bring it up again
lessons.noon: “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.” — Lord, right now I remember your forgiveness of me.

lessons.title: Forgiving Is Not Forgetting
lessons.theme: Forgiveness hands judgment over to God; it does not pretend we were never hurt

v: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.

lessons.still: If forgiveness is still hard for you, don’t blame yourself. Quietly lay your wound open before the Lord and say, “Lord, it still hurts, but I am willing to hand judgment over to you.” Let the Lord lay his hand on the wound.
teach: When a wound heals, it may still leave a scar. Seeing the scar doesn’t mean the wound is still bleeding. Many people think that “forgiving means forgetting,” so every time they recall the past they blame themselves: “I still remember — does that mean I haven’t forgiven?” But memory is not the same as resentment, just as a scar is not the same as a wound.

God says, “I will not remember your sins.” The all-knowing God has not lost his memory; he has chosen not to hold these sins against us any more. Peter says that when Jesus suffered, he “committed himself to him who judges righteously.” That is what forgiveness is: I don’t deny that I was hurt, but I give up my right to collect the debt, and I entrust justice to God.

Forgiveness is also not the same as immediately restoring trust. Forgiveness is a one-sided decision that can begin today; trust is rebuilt by both sides over time, and it needs fruit. A change of mindset: forgiveness does not say, “You did nothing wrong.” It says, “I no longer require you to repay me” — I hand you over to God, and I set myself free from bitterness.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Focus on Jesus — not on others, and not on our own wounds. Handing judgment over to God is returning to our place; only when I let God be God am I set free. Replaying the past in the head brings only worry; living from the heart by the Spirit brings healing from bitterness.
q: Who is God? — God “will not remember” our sins — what kind of grace is that?
Who am I? — Have you mistaken “I still remember” for “I haven’t forgiven yet”?
How shall I respond? — Which debt are you willing to hand over to him who judges righteously?
lessons.jesus: After his resurrection, Jesus still bore the nail marks in his hands and the wound in his side. He did not erase the scars; he made them the grounds for Thomas’s faith. In Jesus’ hands, our scars too can turn from marks of shame into testimonies of grace.
lessons.pray: Lord who judges righteously, I hand over to you my pain and my right to collect the debt. I won’t pretend I was never hurt, but I choose not to hold on to resentment. Heal my wounds and make my scars a testimony to your grace, and give me wisdom to know how to rebuild the relationship. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write: “I forgive ____, and I hand them over to God.”
When the past comes back to mind, pray once instead of replaying it once
Let go of an old grievance against one of “my 2,” and stop dragging it back up
lessons.noon: “But committed himself to him who judges righteously.” — Lord, right now I hand judgment over to you.

lessons.title: Taking the First Step to Restore
lessons.theme: Don’t wait for the other person to come first; Jesus tells us to go

v: “If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
“If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.

lessons.still: Ask the Holy Spirit to bring to mind a relationship that has a crack in it — perhaps you wronged someone, perhaps someone wronged you. Don’t rush to work out who was right and who was wrong; simply ask, “Lord, what small step do you want me to take?”
teach: When a river freezes over, someone has to break the first crack in the ice. When a relationship breaks down, we often wait — for the other person to apologise first, to call first, to back down first. But Jesus gives two scenarios, and the answer to both is the same: “You go.”

In the first scenario, you have wronged someone: “if you… remember that your brother has anything against you,” even worship must pause — “first be reconciled to your brother.” In the second, someone has wronged you: “go, show him his fault between you and him alone.” Whoever is right or wrong, the one who takes the initiative is “you.” The goal is not to win but to have “gained back your brother.”

Restoring a relationship takes wisdom: speak privately, without public shaming; speak about facts, without attacking character; aim to win the person, not to prove yourself right. Sometimes the other person won’t respond, and even so we have done our part. A change of mindset: taking the first step is not losing; it is letting Jesus reign in this relationship.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is the key to revival. Pride waits for the other person to back down first; humility goes and knocks on the door first. Humility draws out humility and both sides win — the one who takes the first step towards reconciliation often opens the other person’s heart. First with God, then with others; being reconciled with others is part of our fellowship with God.
q: Who is God? — God came to reconcile us to himself while we were still his enemies — what does that show you about him?
Who am I? — In which relationship have you been “waiting for the other person to come first”?
How shall I respond? — Towards whom will you take the first step of restoration?
lessons.jesus: While we were still God’s enemies, Jesus took the initiative and came into the world, reconciling us to God through the cross (Romans 5:10). He did not wait for us to apologise first; he paid the price of reconciliation first, and then entrusted to us the ministry of reconciliation. The initiative to reconcile has always been on God’s side.
lessons.pray: Lord, you came first to be reconciled with me, yet I often wait for others to come to me first. Give me humility and courage to take the first step towards that broken relationship. Give me fitting words, so that I seek not to win but to gain back my brother or sister. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Send a message to one of “my 2,” taking the first step to break a chill between you
If you have wronged someone, go and apologise today — with no “but” attached
Pray first for the conversation to restore the relationship, and write down the first sentence you will say
lessons.noon: “First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.” — Lord, right now give me courage to take the first step.

lessons.title: Don’t Hurt People over Things
lessons.theme: Christ died for each person; people are more precious than any task

v: Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Don’t destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
So then, let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.

lessons.still: Recall a recent “thing” that put you in conflict with someone: a plan, an opinion, a way of doing things. Put it in your left hand; put that person in your right hand. Quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, in your eyes, which weighs more?”
teach: A parent yells at a child over a broken vase. The vase cannot be saved, and now the child’s heart is broken too. We often hurt people over things: over a meeting’s decision, a ministry procedure, who was right and who was wrong. The task gets done, but the person walks away. This week we have walked through Joseph’s forgiveness (Day 1), seventy times seven (Day 2), forgiving is not forgetting (Day 3), and taking the first step to restore (Day 4).

The early church argued fiercely over “what to eat.” Paul did not begin by ruling on who was right. He said, “Don’t destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.” That sentence turns the whole matter’s weight upside down — food is a thing, but a brother is a person bought with Christ’s life. So “let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.”

This does not mean tasks are unimportant; it means tasks should serve people, not people be sacrificed for tasks. Next week we will learn about the rhythm of family and work — exactly the place where it is easiest to hurt people over things. A change of mindset: before doing anything, ask, “Will this build people up, or hurt them?”
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things; don’t hurt people over things. Life first, then relationships, then ministry — if ministry damages relationships, it has lost its meaning. God’s kingdom system is built on people who are loved, not on tasks that are completed.
q: Who is God? — “Him for whom Christ died” — how does this change the way you see the person nearby who gives you headaches?
Who am I? — Have you recently hurt someone over some task or issue?
How shall I respond? — How will you put people back in the place where they weigh more than things?
lessons.jesus: On his way to save Jairus’s daughter, Jesus still stopped to seek out, listen to and bless a woman who had suffered from bleeding. He stopped for a blind man crying out by the roadside, and changed his plans for Zacchaeus in the tree. To him, people always mattered more than tasks.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, forgive me for so often hurting people over things, and losing brothers and sisters over who was right. Thank you for laying down your life for every person. Help me to see people as you see them, to love people before doing tasks, and to build people up before insisting on my way. I want to pursue the things that make for peace. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Sincerely apologise to one of “my 2” for a time you hurt them over some task or issue
Before your next meeting or decision, first pray for the people involved
Tomorrow (Saturday), share this week’s lessons on forgiveness with your spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “Let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.” — Lord, right now let me put people before things.

mem.t: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

lessons.title: Unless the Lord Builds
lessons.theme: The worth of our labour lies in whether God himself is building

v: Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

lessons.still: Think of the thing that has made you busiest and most anxious lately. Place it before the Lord and ask, “Lord, are you building this, or am I?” Then relax your shoulders and admit, “Without you, it is all in vain.”
teach: Workers on a building site may carry bricks and lay walls, but without the architect’s blueprint, the faster they build, the harder it will fall. The psalmist uses the word “vain” three times: the builders labour in vain, the watchman guards in vain, rising early and staying up late is in vain. He is not telling people not to work; he is saying that work done apart from God is wasted effort.

“He gives sleep to his loved ones.” The contrast in this verse is stark: on one side, anxiously rising early and staying up late; on the other, peaceful sleep. God does not reward laziness with sleep; he uses sleep to show that he is the one who truly builds. While I sleep, God does not; the world keeps turning in his hands.

This week we learn the rhythm of family and work. Many Christians’ problem is not that they don’t work hard, but that they work too hard — treating themselves as the builder of everything. A change of mindset: from “It all depends on me” to “I work together with God, and God is the builder.” Being able to sleep in peace is itself an expression of faith.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. Anxiety is often an expression of the self-ruled life — I think I have to hold everything together. People living the self-emptied life return to their place, doing what people should do and letting God do what God does. Building God’s kingdom system begins with letting God be the builder.
q: Who is God? — “He gives sleep to his loved ones” — what does this show you about God’s love?
Who am I? — Do you treat yourself as the builder of everything in your life?
How shall I respond? — How will you express your trust tonight by “sleeping in peace”?
lessons.jesus: While the disciples panicked in the storm, Jesus was asleep in the stern on a cushion. It was not that he didn’t care; he trusted the Father completely. He woke, rebuked the wind and the waves, and they stopped, and there was a great calm. In his presence, we too can sleep in peace.
lessons.pray: God who built all things, I confess that I often think everything depends on me, rising early and staying up late, anxious and restless. Today I hand my work, my family and my future over to you. Be the builder, so that I can work together with you and sleep in peace in your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Go to bed thirty minutes earlier than usual tonight, and before sleeping hand tomorrow over to God
Before you start work, pray: “Lord, please build this yourself.”
Share with one of “my 2” something you are learning to entrust to God
lessons.noon: “Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain.” — Lord, right now please build this yourself.

lessons.title: Work Is God’s Calling
lessons.theme: Work is not a curse but a trust: working together with God

v: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.

lessons.still: Picture where you will work today: a desk, a kitchen, a classroom, a building site, or your home. Quietly invite the Lord into that place: “Lord, that place is yours too. Today I go there to work for you.”
teach: Many people see work as a punishment for the Fall, and Monday as the start of the week’s misery. Yet before humanity sinned, God “put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.” Work was God’s original design, not the result of sin. Sin brought thorns and sweat, but work itself is a good trust.

Paul wrote to the slaves of his day — the lowest-ranking workers in society — “Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men.” Even a slave’s work could become service to God, because “you serve the Lord Christ.” Your boss sees your performance; the Lord sees your heart.

A change of mindset: there is no division between “spiritual work” and “secular work,” only between work done “for the Lord” and work done “for myself.” Cleaning, bookkeeping, teaching, caring for children — all of it can be worship. When work becomes a calling, we no longer work to prove ourselves, nor do we procrastinate to escape it.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A shift in perspective — from the worldly to the godly. On the path of service, serving means letting Jesus reign and serving by his authority. When we let Jesus reign in the workplace, our work becomes a place for building God’s kingdom system. The glory is not mine; it belongs to Jesus.
q: Who is God? — God himself is at work in creating, sustaining and redeeming — how does this shape the way you see your own work?
Who am I? — Do you work for the Lord, for other people’s approval, or to prove yourself?
How shall I respond? — In which task today will you work “as for the Lord”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My Father is still working, so I am working too” (John 5:17). In Nazareth he worked as a carpenter, making ploughs and yokes with his hands; in his ministry he went through all the towns and villages. His work was never for his own name, but to finish what the Father had entrusted to him.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for entrusting work to me. Forgive me for so often complaining about my work, or treating it as a place to prove myself. Today, whatever I do, I will work at it with all my heart, as for you. Reign in my work. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before you start work, write: “Today I am working for the Lord.”
Wholeheartedly complete a piece of work no one will notice
Say a word of thanks for their hard work to one of “my 2” (a colleague or family member)
lessons.noon: “And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men” — Lord, right now I do this for you.

lessons.title: The Priority of Family
lessons.theme: The family is the first spiritual community God established

v: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

lessons.still: In your heart, bring each member of your family to mind, one by one. Pause quietly at each name and ask the Lord, “Lord, lately have I been giving them my best time, or my leftover time?”
teach: Many people give their best energy to work and bring their leftover exhaustion home — like a chef who prepares a banquet for customers at the restaurant, then goes home and feeds the family instant noodles. That is not God’s intention. Before the tabernacle and the temple, God first established the family in Eden.

Moses commanded that God’s words be taught “diligently to your children, and… when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.” Passing on the faith does not happen only once a week in a church building, but at the dinner table, on the road, and at bedtime. Paul puts it even more seriously: whoever does not provide for his own household “is worse than an unbeliever.”

The order of relationships: first with God, then with myself, then with others, then with things. Our family are the “others” closest to us, and they come before things. This doesn’t mean work is unimportant, but work should not swallow up the family. A change of mindset: the family is not an obstacle to ministry; it is the first workshop of ministry.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. The family is the most real training ground for 920 — my family are my closest 2. Living the self-emptied life at home is harder than living it on the platform, and more genuine. A family built on God’s word is itself part of God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — God established the family before he established the temple — what does this show you about what God values?
Who am I? — Are you giving your family your best time, or your leftover time?
How shall I respond? — What uninterrupted time will you set aside for your family this week?
lessons.jesus: In the terrible agony of the cross, Jesus still saw his mother and entrusted her to the care of the disciple he loved. Even at the moment of completing the great work of redemption, he did not neglect his family. His ministry never came at the cost of sacrificing his family.
lessons.pray: Father, thank you for giving me a family. Forgive me for so often giving my family my leftover time. Help me, at the table, on the road and at bedtime, to bring your word and your love to my family. Reign in my home. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Share a meal with your family today without looking at your phone
Before bed, pray briefly for each member of your family
Say a word of thanks or apology to one of “my 2” (a family member)
lessons.noon: “These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart.” — Lord, right now let your word live in my home.

lessons.title: Rest in the Midst of Work
lessons.theme: Only one thing is needed: sitting at the Lord’s feet

v: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,

lessons.still: Stop what you are doing, and sit at the Lord’s feet like Mary. Do nothing; simply be in his presence. If items from your to-do list pop up, don’t chase them away; just lay them, one by one, at the Lord’s feet.
teach: When your phone’s battery is low, no amount of effort will keep it going for long; you have to plug it in. Martha was a hard-working woman, and preparing a meal for Jesus was a good thing. But she was “anxious and troubled about many things,” to the point of blaming her sister and challenging Jesus. Her problem was not her work; it was that she lost the Lord in the middle of it.

Jesus said, “One thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part.” Isaiah also said, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” Sadly, Israel “refused.” Strength does not come from busyness; it comes from returning to God and being still before him.

Resting in the midst of work does not mean not working; it means keeping our hearts with the Lord while we work. Work can include short pauses: an arrow prayer, a deep breath, a verse of Scripture. A change of mindset: rest is not the reward after the work is finished; it is the source of the work. First sit at the Lord’s feet, then rise to serve.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself — from the heart comes joy, from the head comes worry. Martha lived from her head and grew more troubled the more she did; Mary lived from her heart and received the good part. With our focus on Jesus rather than on tasks, our work can become service that flows from rest.
q: Who is God? — Jesus tenderly called, “Martha, Martha” — how does he see you in your busyness?
Who am I? — In your work or ministry, are you more like Martha or like Mary?
How shall I respond? — What moment of “sitting at the Lord’s feet” will you build into your work today?
lessons.jesus: At the busiest point of Jesus’ ministry, so many people were coming and going that there was no time even to eat, yet he often withdrew to deserted places to pray. He drew strength from the Father, then went out again to serve the crowds. He was busy, but his heart was never in a panic, because his source was in the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that I am often like Martha, anxious and troubled about many things. Call me by name and bring me back to your feet. I choose the good part, and even in my work I will not leave your presence. Be the source of my strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set a reminder every three hours to stop and pray a one-line arrow prayer
Write down the things that make you “anxious and troubled,” and hand them to the Lord one by one
Instead of hurrying one of “my 2,” invite them to stop with you for a cup of tea
lessons.noon: “But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part” — Lord, right now I sit at your feet.

lessons.title: The Rhythm of Day and Night
lessons.theme: The rhythm God has set is a protection for our lives

v: God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

lessons.still: Notice your breathing: in and out, in and out. Life has a rhythm built into it. Quietly ask the Lord, “Lord, is the rhythm of my life within your design, or has it lost its balance?”
teach: The heart contracts and relaxes; breathing goes in and out; land is farmed and then left fallow. This week we have seen that God is the builder (Day 1), that work is a calling (Day 2), the priority of family (Day 3), and rest in the midst of work (Day 4). Today we learn the rhythm God has set.

Genesis says, “There was evening and there was morning, the first day.” For the Hebrews, the day began in the evening — first rest, then work. While we sleep, God is already at work. Jesus also said to his busy disciples, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” Rest is not laziness; it is the Lord’s own invitation.

God established the Sabbath to protect people with time, so that we remember: I am not a machine; I am a child of God. Next week is the Stage 3 retreat week, when we will stop to review the fruit of these thirteen weeks. A change of mindset: rhythm is not wasted time; it is essential for a life that bears lasting fruit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. People who never stop working are often trying to hold up the world in God’s place; those who are willing to stop are acknowledging that God is the one in control. Rest is trust in God, and a form of worship that lets Jesus receive all the glory.
q: Who is God? — God established day and night and the Sabbath — what does this show you about his heart?
Who am I? — Does your life have a rhythm of breathing in and out, or is it all breathing in and never out?
How shall I respond? — What time of rest will you set for yourself and your family this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus himself lived in rhythm: teaching and healing among the crowds by day, going out to deserted places to pray in the early morning; sometimes with the many, sometimes withdrawing with just his disciples. He was never frantic and never stagnant, because his steps were in step with the Father’s heart.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for setting the rhythm of day and night and of Sabbath rest. Forgive me for so often working without resting, as if everything depended on me. I accept your invitation to come apart with you to a deserted place and rest awhile. Reorder the rhythm of my life, and let me find strength in you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set aside a full block of Sabbath rest this week, and put it in your calendar
Turn off your screens before bed tonight, and end the day with thanksgiving
Invite one of “my 2” (a family member or co-worker) to enjoy some time of rest together
lessons.noon: “Come away into a deserted place” — Lord, right now I rest awhile in you.

mem.t: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

lessons.title: Nine Fruits, One Life
lessons.theme: The nine fruits are not nine assignments but the one life of Christ

v: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

lessons.still: Slowly read the nine fruits aloud: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Pause after each one, and recall one way the Lord has spoken to you about that fruit during this stage.
teach: This is the retreat week of Stage 3, “Fruiting: The 920 Practice.” Thirteen weeks ago we set out from “everyone is my 2,” then practised the nine fruits one by one, and finally learned about forgiveness and restoration and the rhythm of life. This week we stop, like a farmer looking back at harvest time, to count: what fruit has the Lord produced in me?

Notice that the word Paul uses for “fruit” is singular in the original. The nine fruits are not nine separate virtues from which we can pick a few to work on; they are nine aspects of one life — like a bunch of grapes with many grapes, all growing on the same branch. That life is Christ himself: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.”

So the point of our review is not “How well have I done?” but “Have I been remaining in the Lord?” When there is little fruit, the reason is not too little effort but too little connection. “Apart from me you can do nothing” — this is not only a warning; it is also a promise: joined to the Lord, we will surely bear fruit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Fruit is the life of Christ flowing naturally from those who live the self-emptied life; it is not produced by our own self-improvement. Self-ruled people try to “manufacture” fruit and end up exhausted and fake; people living the self-emptied life abide in the Lord, and the fruit grows naturally. Let Jesus receive all the glory — even our fruit is his.
q: Who is God? — The vine supplies everything the branches need — what does this show you about the Lord?
Who am I? — Of the nine fruits, which has grown most visibly in you during this stage? Which most needs to grow?
How shall I respond? — How will you “remain in the Lord” more deeply?
lessons.jesus: The nine fruits are fully displayed in Jesus: he loved to the end; he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit; he gave people peace; he was patient through it all; he was kind to sinners; he went about doing good; he is faithful and true; he is gentle and humble in heart; and he obeyed perfectly in temptation. He is the true vine.
lessons.pray: Lord, the true vine, thank you for working in me during this stage. I confess that apart from you I can do nothing; all fruit is your life. Help me to remain in you more deeply, and let the nine fruits flow out of my life more abundantly, all to your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the nine fruits, and beside each one write an experience from this stage
Memorise this week’s verse: Galatians 5:22–23
Share with one of “my 2” one fruit the Lord has produced in you
lessons.noon: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” — Lord, right now I remain in you.

lessons.title: How My 2 Have Changed
lessons.theme: Love is seen in relationships, and that is where disciples are recognised

v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

lessons.still: Take out the “my 2” list you wrote in Week 27 (if you don’t have one, list them in your mind). Pause quietly at each name, and reflect: what has changed between us during this stage?
teach: A mirror can’t show you the back of your head; sometimes we only see how we have really changed through other people’s eyes. The best report card for this stage’s practice is not in our own notebooks but in the lives of our 2: Does my family find me gentler? Do my colleagues find me more reliable?

Jesus said, “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” The mark of a disciple is not knowledge, not gifts, not how many meetings we attend, but love. And this love has a standard: “Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.” This love must be seen in real, specific people.

Be honest as you review: some relationships have improved, some are still hard, and some may even be more tense. Don’t be discouraged, and don’t boast. Relationships often change slowly, like the turning of the seasons. What matters is this: have I begun to see my 2 through Christ’s eyes? A changed life changes relationships.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fivefold change — mindset, life, lifestyle, relationships, ministry. The practice of 920 is letting the change in our lives flow into our relationships. Every person in my life is my 2; when I live out the “0” of the self-emptied life, they will see the “9” of Christ in me.
q: Who is God? — Jesus says, “Just as I have loved you” — how has he loved you during this stage?
Who am I? — In the eyes of your 2, how have you changed during this stage?
How shall I respond? — Which of your 2 will you take special care to love in the next stage?
lessons.jesus: Jesus walked with his disciples for three years. His love was not from a distance; it was lived out eating together, walking together, being misunderstood together. On the last night, he washed his disciples’ feet, showing them by his actions what “just as I have loved you” means.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for loving me with your love, and for placing my 2 in my life. For the relationships that have changed, I give you the glory; the ones that are still hard, I place in your hands. Let everyone recognise by my love that I am your disciple. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Review your “my 2” list, and beside each name write one change
Ask a family member or close friend: “How do you think I have changed over this time?”
Write a thank-you card to one of “my 2,” thanking them for growing alongside you
lessons.noon: “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” — Lord, right now let people recognise you in me.

lessons.title: Testimonies of Grace in Relationships
lessons.theme: By the grace of God I am what I am

v: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

lessons.still: Recall a moment of grace in one of your relationships during this stage: an act of forgiveness, a reconciliation, a gentle word, a patient evening. Don’t analyse it; simply give thanks, and let that grace warm your heart once more.
teach: The moon gives no light of its own; its light is reflected from the sun. When people see moonlight at night, they are really seeing the sun. Paul says, “We all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory.” The changes in our relationships are a reflection of the Lord’s glory.

Paul looked back on the change in his own life: from persecutor of the church to apostle of the gospel. He said, “By the grace of God I am what I am.” He admitted that he “worked more than all of them,” but immediately added, “yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.” The point of a testimony is not what I have done but what grace has done.

Today, prepare a “testimony of grace in a relationship”: what the relationship was like before, how God stepped in, and what has changed now. Keep it simple and true, and give the glory to God. A testimony is not showing off spiritual achievements; it lets people see that the God who could change me can change you too. This is also the first step towards multiplying.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let Jesus receive all the glory. A self-ruled testimony exalts our own effort; a self-emptied testimony exalts God’s grace. The last step on the path of service is “God” — giving glory to God and giving thanks in everything. A testimony offers the fruit of our relationships back to the Lord.
q: Who is God? — “Even as from the Lord, the Spirit” — who does this show you is the source of change?
Who am I? — In which relationship have you seen God’s grace most clearly?
How shall I respond? — How will you share this testimony so that the Lord is glorified?
lessons.jesus: After Jesus healed the man possessed by demons, he said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.” Testimonies of grace begin in our closest relationships.
lessons.pray: Lord of grace, by your grace I am what I am. Thank you for working in my relationships and freeing me, little by little, from the bondage of the self-ruled life. Let my testimony never exalt myself, but help people see your work that goes from glory to glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a three-part testimony: what it was like before, how God stepped in, and how it is now
Share this testimony of grace with one of “my 2”
Offer a prayer of thanksgiving for all of your 2
lessons.noon: “But by the grace of God I am what I am.” — Lord, right now all the glory is yours.

lessons.title: Stage Self-Review
lessons.theme: Honest review before God is for renewal, not condemnation

v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

lessons.still: Quietly invite the Holy Spirit to shine into your heart like a gentle light. Say, “Search me, God.” Don’t rush to give yourself a score; first sit a while before the Lord, remembering that you are his beloved child, and only then begin your self-review.
teach: The purpose of a health check-up is not to frighten us but to catch problems early and treat them properly. The Stage 3 spiritual health self-review is the same: we are not handing God a report card; we are telling the Doctor honestly how we are, so that he can heal, adjust, and guide our next steps.

David prayed, “Search me, God, and know my heart… See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.” He did not search himself; he asked God to search him. As you review yourself, let the Holy Spirit lead you, not your own feelings. Paul also says, “He who began a good work in you will complete it.”

As you review, you might ask: Is my relationship with God closer than it was thirteen weeks ago? Of the nine fruits, which has grown most and which least? How have my relationships with my 2 changed? Am I more able to forgive, and does my life have more rhythm? Answer honestly, then hand the results to the God who will surely complete the good work he began.
lessons.light: 321 Light: These are the “Review” and “Correction” steps of the eight steps for changing our mindset. Self-review is not self-blame; it is reviewing in grace and correcting under the Holy Spirit’s guidance, so that we can keep practising and move towards multiplication. Keep your focus on Jesus; he will complete the work he began.
q: Who is God? — “Will complete it” — how do you trust this God who never gives up halfway?
Who am I? — During this stage, what growth are you most grateful for? And what do you most need?
How shall I respond? — Based on your self-review, what one thing will you adjust in the next stage?
lessons.jesus: By the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” It was not an interrogation; it was helping Peter face himself honestly, and then entrusting him again: “Feed my sheep.” The Lord’s searching always comes with a call to renewal.
lessons.pray: Search me, God, and know my heart; see if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way. I hand over to you both my growth and my shortcomings in this stage. Thank you for beginning a good work in me; you will surely complete it. Guide my next step. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Complete this stage's spiritual health self-review
Write down the growth you are most grateful for, and one area to adjust
Ask one of “my 2”: “In what area do you think I can still grow?”
lessons.noon: “Search me, God, and know my heart.” — Lord, right now I open myself before you.

lessons.title: Resolving to Multiply
lessons.theme: Bearing fruit is not the finish line; the fruit is meant to last

v: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.

lessons.still: Quietly consider: of the fruit the Lord has produced in me during this stage, which could become a seed in someone else’s life? Bring one person’s face to mind and ask, “Lord, use me to be a blessing in their life.”
teach: An apple holds several seeds; each one could grow into a tree, and each tree could bear many apples. The ultimate purpose of fruit is not to be admired but to multiply. This week we have reviewed the nine fruits (Day 1), how my 2 have changed (Day 2), testimonies of grace (Day 3), and the stage self-review (Day 4).

Jesus said, “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit.” And again, “I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain.” Fruit that “remains” does not wither after one season; it is life passing on life, generation after generation. This is the Lord’s own choosing and appointing, not our own ambition.

In the next stage, we move from Fruiting to Multiplying: from bearing fruit ourselves to helping others bear fruit too; from being accompanied to accompanying others. Life first, then relationships, then ministry — having Christ’s life and having borne fruit in our relationships, we can now multiply naturally. You don’t need to be perfect; you only need to be willing.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose — to build what belongs to God. The nine fruits in one person are a testimony; in many people, they become a display of the kingdom. In the next stage, the 235 journey begins: 2 spiritual companions, 3 spiritual parents and children, 5 fellow soldiers. Let Jesus receive all the glory.
q: Who is God? — The Lord has “chosen” and “appointed” you to bear fruit — how does this change the way you see your life?
Who am I? — Do you think you are not yet good enough to help others?
How shall I respond? — What resolution will you make as you enter the next stage of multiplying?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.” He himself is that grain of wheat: he died and rose again, and bore countless grains — including you and me. The road to multiplication is the road of the self-emptied life.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for choosing me and appointing me to bear fruit. All the fruit of this stage is your grace. I resolve to enter the next stage, not only bearing fruit myself but also willing to become a seed in other people’s lives. Make my fruit remain, so that the Father is glorified. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a one-sentence resolution: “In the next stage, I am willing to…”
Say to one of “my 2”: “I’d love to grow in the Lord together with you.”
Pray with your spiritual companion, entrusting the next stage to the Lord
lessons.noon: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit.” — Lord, right now I want to bear fruit that remains.
